newsitem.title: UK: Russia MinFins to be main beneficiary of Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Russia MinFins to be main beneficiary of Eurobond.

text.p: Russian MinFins are set to be the main beneficiaries of the country's debut Eurobond, but analysts caution that the sheer size of the issue means there may be little immediate spillover in to the market.
"With a $1.0 billion issue, much of the immediate demand for Russia will have been satisified," said Philip Poole head of emerging market economic research at ING Barings in London.

MinFins tightened in early London trade, but came off their highs in relatively light trade, but analysts believes that the Eurobond and unfreezing of certain MinFin issues creates room for further rises.

"I would far rather own say the MinFin threes than the Eurobond which was priced at 345 basis points over U.S. Treasuries," said Paul Luke head of emerging debt research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
"The holding returns on the MinFins are so strong that it would require a 700 basis point rise in yields to wipe them out," said Luke.
MinFin threes were quoted up 3/4 of a point in early London trade at 83 3/4 bid, the fours were up half a point at 60 3/4.
"There is plenty of room for this market to appreciate. It is going to be the market of 1997," said ING's Poole.

On the back of Russia's Eurobond success, other issues are expected, Moscow city is set for an offering, Nizhny Novogorod also plans a Eurobond as does the railway system. The state is also expected to return to western capital markets.
"Any new isssues will just bring Russia to a level of external debt which is commensurate with the size of the economy," said Jonathan Hoffman, head of emerging market economics at CS First Boston.
